'''Donald Gene Truhlar''' (born 27 February 1944, Chicago) is an American scientist working in theoretical and [[computational chemistry]] and chemical physics with special emphases on quantum mechanics and chemical dynamics.<ref>http://pubs.acs.org/toc/jpcafh/110/2 Journal of Physical Chemistry A Volume 110, Issue 2, 2006: Donald G. Truhlar Festschrift</ref>

==Early life, education, and early work==
Donald Gene Truhlar was born in [[Chicago]] on 27 February 1944 to John Joseph Truhlar<ref>{{Cite web |title=John Truhlar Obituary (2006) - Denver, CO - Denver Post |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/denverpost/name/john-truhlar-obituary?id=26108893 |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=Legacy.com}}</ref> and Lucille Marie Vancura,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lucille Truhlar Obituary (2002) - Denver, CO - Denver Post |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/denverpost/name/lucille-truhlar-obituary?id=27978944 |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=Legacy.com}}</ref> both of [[Czechs|Czech]] ancestry.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Truhlar |date=1930 |title=United States Census, 1930 |url=https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XSL3-5BJ |website=FamilySearch}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Vancura |date=1930 |title=United States Census, 1930 |url=https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XSRG-DGG |website=FamilySearch}}</ref> Truhlar received a B.A., from [[St. Mary's College of Minnesota]] (1965), and a Ph.D., from [[Caltech]] (1970), under  [[Aron Kuppermann]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cce.caltech.edu/faculty/kuppermann/index.html |title=FACULTY ::: Division of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering ::: CALTECH |access-date=2012-03-12 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120306162933/http://www.cce.caltech.edu/faculty/kuppermann/index.html |archive-date=2012-03-06 }}</ref> He has been on the faculty of the [[University of Minnesota]] since 1969.

==Important contributions==
Truhlar is known for his contributions<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.iaqms.org/members/truhlar.php | title=International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science}}</ref> to theoretical chemical dynamics of chemical reactions; quantum mechanical [[Scattering|scattering theory]] of chemical reactions and molecular energy transfer; electron scattering; theoretical [[Chemical kinetics|kinetics]] and chemical dynamics; [[potential energy surface]]s and molecular interactions; [[Path integral Monte Carlo|path integrals]]; variational [[transition state]] theory; the use of electronic structure theory for calculations of chemical structure, reaction rates, electronically nonadiabatic processes, and solvation effects; [[photochemistry]]; [[Combustion|combustion chemistry]]; heterogeneous, homogeneous, and enzyme [[catalysis]]; atmospheric and environmental chemistry; [[drug design]]; nanoparticle structure and energetics; [[Basis set (chemistry)|basis set]] development; and [[density functional theory]], including the [[Minnesota Functionals]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Zhao |first1=Yan |last2=Truhlar |first2=Donald G. |date=2008-05-01 |title=The M06 suite of density functionals for main group thermochemistry, thermochemical kinetics, noncovalent interactions, excited states, and transition elements: two new functionals and systematic testing of four M06-class functionals and 12 other functionals |journal=Theoretical Chemistry Accounts |language=en |volume=120 |issue=1 |pages=215–241 |doi=10.1007/s00214-007-0310-x |issn=1432-2234|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=1gaf87YAAAAJ|title=Donald Truhlar}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Truhlar was elected to the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]] (2006), the [[National Academy of Sciences]] of the USA (2009), and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (2015). He became an Honorary Fellow of the [[Chinese Chemical Society (Beijing)|Chinese Chemical Society]] in 2015. He was named a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], (1986) the [[American Chemical Society]] (2009), the [[American Physical Society]] (1986), the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (2009), and the [[World Association of Theoretical and Computational Chemists]] (2006). He was a visiting fellow at the [[Battelle Memorial Institute]] (1973) and at the [[Joint Institute for Laboratory Astrophysics]] (1975–76), and was named an [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Alfred P. Sloan Foundation Research Fellow]] (1973).

He received the NSF Creativity Award (1993), the ACS Award for Computers in Chemical and Pharmaceutical Research (2000), the Minnesota Award (2003) ("for outstanding contributions to the chemical sciences"), the National Academy of Sciences Award for Scientific Reviewing (2004); the ACS [[Peter Debye Award]] for Physical Chemistry (2006), the Lise Meitner Lectureship Award (2006), the Schrödinger Medal of The World Association of Theoretical and Computational Chemists (2006), the Dudley R. Herschbach Award for Research in Molecular Collision Dynamics (2009), Doctor honoris causa of Technical University of Lodz, Poland, (2010), the Royal Society of Chemistry Chemical Dynamics Award (2012), the APS Earle K. Plyler Prize for Molecular Spectroscopy and Dynamics (2015), the 2019 ACS Award in Theoretical Chemistry (2018),<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://chem.umn.edu/news/professor-truhlar-receives-2019-acs-award-theoretical-chemistry|title=Professor Truhlar receives 2019 ACS Award in Theoretical Chemistry|date=2018-09-17|work=Department of Chemistry|access-date=2018-09-24|language=en}}</ref> and the 2023 [[Joseph O. Hirschfelder]] Prize in Theoretical Chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Regents Professor Donald Truhlar awarded Joseph O. Hirschfelder Prize in Theoretical Chemistry |url=https://cse.umn.edu/chem/news/regents-professor-donald-truhlar-awarded-joseph-o-hirschfelder-prize-theoretical |access-date=2023-09-18 |website=College of Science and Engineering, University of Minnesota |language=en}}</ref>

Truhlar has served as an associate editor of the ''[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]'' (1984–2016), as (successively) editor, editor-in-chief, associate editor, and chief advisory editor of Theoretical Chemistry Accounts (formerly ''[[Theoretica Chimica Acta]]'') (1985–present), and as a principal editor of '' [[Computer Physics Communications]]'' (1986–2015).<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1021/jp055732y | volume=110 | issue=2 | title=Curriculum Vitae of Donald G. Truhlar | journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry A | pages=359–360| year=2006 | bibcode=2006JPCA..110..359. }}</ref> He is currently a Regents professor at the University of Minnesota, which is the university's highest honor.<ref>{{cite web |title=Regents Professorship |url=https://uawards.umn.edu/university-awards/regents-professorship |publisher=University of Minnesota |access-date=24 July 2023}}</ref> The University of Minnesota has also honored him as a Distinguished University Teaching Professor and a College of Science & Engineering Distinguished Professor.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Donald G. Truhlar |url=https://cse.umn.edu/chem/donald-g-truhlar |access-date=2024-05-24 |website=cse.umn.edu |language=en}}</ref>
